question: Should OpenClaw adopt first-declaration exact-path ownership, immutable layered mode, and the narrow monotonic tool-policy exceptions as its permanent managed-configuration contract?
rationale: This introduces a new core CLI/configuration mode and durable authority and security semantics; testing can prove implementation behavior but cannot choose the product contract.

options.title: Approve the V1 contract
options.body: Accept the startup-only model as written and coordinate RFC acceptance with the linked implementation.

options.title: Revise authority semantics
options.body: Keep both drafts open while maintainers change precedence, mutability, conflict handling, or monotonic-policy rules.

options.title: Decline core layering
options.body: Retain host-side composition instead of adding this contract to OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Approve the V1 contract
recommendation.body: Accept the startup-only model as written and coordinate RFC acceptance with the linked implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent configuration I/O, runtime, and security history makes Vincent the strongest available routing candidate for this cross-cutting contract decision.
